sentences.text: 3 09-05-2025 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
2. This is the first regular bail application of the petitioner seeking his regular bail in connection with Lakhisarai (Kabaiya) P.S. Case No. 111 of 2024 registered for the offence under Sections 406,
420 and 409 of the Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. According to the case of prosecution, one Niraj Kumar made a written complaint against the present applicant before one Abhinash Kumar, Sub-Planning Officer, Lakhisarai wherein it is alleged that the present applicant cheated with the complainant Niraj Kumar of Rs. 25,60,000/- on the assurance of arranging contract work for him.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
It is further alleged that total Rs. 5,84,000/- were transferred to the account of the present Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.7645 of 2025(3)
dt.09-05-2025 applicant from the account of Niraj Kumar on various dates and on the basis of the said written complaint, report has been lodged by Abhinash Kumar, on the basis of which, offence has been registered.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
During course of investigation, the present applicant is arrested on 24.04.2024.
4.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case due to some family dispute with Niraj Kumar.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no material available on record, which prima facie established that any crime of cheating has been committed by the petitioner herein.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: He further submits that though in paragraph no. 53 of the case diary, it is mentioned that on some occasions, some money have been transferred in the account of the present applicant through online, but the statements of account of the present applicant and the complainant Niraj Kumar have not been collected by the prosecution at the time of investigation.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Charge sheet was filed without collecting those statements, therefore, the offence under Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code is also not made out against the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Lastly, he submits that petitioner is in custody since 24.04.2024 and trial is still going on and it will take some more time.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, on these grounds, it is prayed that the petitioner may Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.7645 of 2025(3) dt.09-05-2025 be granted benefit of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the State opposes the arguments raised by the counsel for the petitioner and submits that in the confessional statement, the applicant admitted his guilt, therefore on this ground, his prayer for bail may be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Heard 7.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Perused the case diary and other materials available on record.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. Taking into consideration the above submissions made by the counsel for the petitioner and further taking to the fact that the petitioner is in custody since 24.04.2024, I am of the view that it is a case where the petitioner should be granted benefit of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. Accordingly, the application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
10. Let the petitioner, above named, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of C.J.M., Lakhisarai in connection with Lakhisarai (Kabaiya) P.S. Case No. 111 of 2024.

sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner in this application prays for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in connection with Dhaka P.S. Case no.466 of 2023 registered for the offence punishable under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. As per the prosecution case, informant namely Shamim Akhtar, alleged that on 11.03.2021 after paying full consideration money informant purchased land from Md. Hussain and has full title and possession over the land.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: But after some time, all named accused persons started creating disturbance and threatened to dispossess the informant on the ground that the land in question has already been purchased by them from Antima Tiwari.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is alleged that accused persons Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.22059 of 2025(3) dt.10-07-2025 under a conspiracy fraudulently on the basis of forged documents purchased the land in question.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he has been falsely implicated in this case merely because he happens to be husband of co-accused Antima Tiwari.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Dispute is purely civil in nature.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: He is neither vendor nor vendee.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Informant has already filed a Title Suit (Title Suit No. 139/2023)
before sub- Judge, East Champaran for the cancellation of sale deed.
sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
He also submits that co-accused Antima Tiwari has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41924054/

sentences._hearing_file: Rupesh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Considering the nature of dispute which is primarily civil in nature and one co-accused has already been granted bail by this Court, it is directed that the petitioner above named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of eight weeks, be released on anticipatory bail in connection with Dhaka P.S. Case no.466 of 2023 on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Patna High Court CR.
